message:
docs: reorganize project and package guidance

- Add contributor, architecture, and getting-started guides with practical workflows
- Refresh product, design, publishing, and package docs; consolidate workshop checks
- Clarify component catalog details and example audio setup

chore(release): 0.3.0

Bump mizu-ui to 0.3.0 and date the changelog's Unreleased section
2026-10-23. It is a minor release: Drawer, Popover, OneTimeCode,
DateRangeField, Dock and LinkProvider are new, Nav, Accordion,
SectionTag, CodeBlock and CommandPalette take new props, and every
export and entry point of 0.2.1 remains.

PUBLISHING.md asks pre-1.0 minor releases for migration notes, so the
section gains them: GhostWord's inline default size, Marquee's item
gap, the line height .mizu-root now sets, Tabs opening on their first
tab, and the registry items renamed to kebab case.

fix(blocks): stop naming each showcase like the block inside it

Each showcase section was a region named by its heading, and the
installable block inside carries the same name, so landmarks listed
"Workspace settings" twice. The block keeps the name; the showcase is
layout with a heading.

feat(site): suggest the closest components on a 404

A miss under /components is usually a mistyped or borrowed name. The
not-found page now names up to three close matches from the search
index (sheet finds Drawer, kanban finds Board) and offers the collection
beside the way back to the archive.

feat(site): find components by the names people already use

Developers arriving from other libraries search for a sheet, a sonner or
an input-otp. Give the search index a short list of those names per
component and match them in ⌘K without showing them.

feat(command-palette): match hidden keywords

People search by the names they already know. Let a command carry
keywords that match without being displayed.

fix(skeleton): put the loading label in the live region's text

Like Spinner, Skeleton named its status region but gave it no text, so
its label was rarely announced. Add the label as visually hidden text and
scope the bar styles to the decorative spans.

fix(lab): send visitors to the collection, not the workshop

The lab closed with "More instruments are in the workshop", but the
workshop is now the theme builder and playground. Say that most of these
ship in mizu-ui and link the collection, filtered to its instruments.

fix(site): tint the browser chrome with the chosen theme

theme-color stayed the dark ink after switching to light, so mobile
browsers kept a black status bar over a paper page. Set it from the
stored theme on load and whenever the theme switches.

fix(cursor): draw the ring from theme tokens

The custom cursor's ring was set in the dark theme's paper at 35%, so on
a light page it was cream on cream and vanished, now that every page can
switch theme. Color it from --mizu-paper and --mizu-accent in CSS, and
leave Motion to animate only its size.

docs: record the co-founder pass decisions and new conventions

Note the new systems and site features in PRODUCT.md as Claude's
delegated choices, and add the drawer, popover, link and bar-action
conventions to DESIGN.md.

docs(catalog): document Drawer, Popover and OneTimeCode

Give the three new systems catalog entries with working examples, props,
accessibility and motion notes, so they get pages, live demos, Markdown
and registry items (drawer, popover, one-time-code). The inventory now
counts 131 systems; the guide reads its count from the catalog instead
of a typed number.

feat(one-time-code): take a sign-in code one digit to a cell

Draw the code as cells over a single native input with
autocomplete=one-time-code and a numeric keyboard, so SMS and email
autofill, paste and screen readers work as they do anywhere. It keeps
digits only, which lets codes pasted with spaces or dashes through, and
calls onComplete at full length. The cells shrink to fit a 320px phone.

feat(popover): open a small panel beside its button

Settings and column pickers need a panel that stays with its button and
gets out of the way. Popover uses the native Popover API, so Escape and
clicking away close it and return focus to the button, and positions
itself below or above the button, flipping when there is no room and
following it as the page scrolls.

feat(drawer): slide a dialog in from an edge

Filters, details and quick edits want a panel at the side of the work,
not a box in the middle of it. Drawer is Dialog with a side (right, left
or bottom) and a slide from that edge, so it keeps the native modal's
focus containment, Escape, inert page and scroll lock. Side drawers
leave 48px of the page on a phone to tap away.

fix(spinner): put the loading label in the live region's text

The status span carried its label only as aria-label, but live regions
announce content, so a spinner appearing often said nothing. Add the
label as visually hidden text and scope the spin to the diamond.

feat(docs): keep collection filters in the URL; forgive plurals

The collection's search and family lived in memory, so a filtered view
couldn't be shared and was lost on Back. Read and write them as ?q= and
?family= with replaceState. Both the collection and the sidebar filter
now match every word in any order and accept plurals, so "charts" finds
BarChart and the sidebar no longer wants a phrase verbatim.

feat(docs): copy any component page as Markdown

Every component already had a Markdown twin at /components/<slug>.md for
agents, but no page pointed to it. Add a quiet row under the tagline that
copies it (through a promised ClipboardItem, so Safari keeps the user
gesture) or opens it.

feat(site): search everything with ⌘K, and switch themes anywhere

Add a search action to the bar that opens Mizu's CommandPalette over
every page and component (Ctrl K off Apple devices). The component index
is a static JSON route fetched on first intent, so pages carry no extra
weight. The theme switch moves from the docs sidebar and workshop header
into the bar, where every page has it, and the bar falls back to the
Menu button below 1024px so the links and actions fit.

fix(command-palette): hold the field still while results narrow

The palette was centred like any dialog, so each keystroke that
shortened the list moved the input. Anchor it near the top of the
window.

feat(nav): keep an actions slot in the bar at every width

Nav had nowhere for controls such as search or a theme switch, and the
menu overlay only lists links. Add actions, grouped with the links and
the Menu button at the right so they stay together whether the chapter
label is showing or not.

fix(command-palette): match each word and open fresh

The query was matched as one phrase, so "range date" missed
DateRangeField, and a query typed before closing came back on reopening.
Require every word anywhere in the label or description, and clear the
query whenever the palette closes.

feat(site): navigate the primary nav without reloading the page

The nav and every ButtonLink did full document loads while the rest of
the site used client navigation. Provide next/link to Mizu's links, and
mark the root so route changes scroll to the top instantly while
in-page anchors keep their smooth scroll.

feat(link-provider): route Mizu's links through the app's router

Nav, Breadcrumbs, SideNav, BottomNav and ButtonLink rendered bare
anchors, so in a routed app every click reloaded the document. Add
LinkProvider, which hands them the app's link component through context
(anchors remain the default), ship it as a registry item, and document
it for Next.js and React Router.

feat(accordion): open items from state and set the heading level

Accordion kept its open set private, so nothing could start open or be
driven from outside, and every title was an h3 whatever the page. Add
value, defaultValue and onValueChange in the shape the other systems
use, and a level prop for the headings.

fix(footer): send Back to top to the page, focus included

The button forced a smooth scroll even under reduced motion, and left
keyboard focus at the foot of the page, so the next Tab stayed there.
Make it a link to #main: the page's scroll-behavior decides the motion,
and the browser moves the focus starting point to the top. It also
takes a 44px target.

fix(docs): give small docs links a 44px target

The previous/next links were 17px tall, "Open full source" and the
sidebar's collection link 20px, and the source disclosure's summary
20px. Make them 44px tall without moving the layout.

fix(home): list all four examples beside the examples link

The note under the signature systems still named three examples after
the audio workbench became the fourth.

fix(site): let buttons be called what they say

Six ButtonLinks passed a label that replaced their visible text for
assistive technology: "Enter the lab" was announced as "The lab", and
"Back to the archive" as "Home", so speech-input users couldn't say
what they saw (WCAG 2.5.3). Drop those labels, stop modelling the prop on
a link with text in the Button usage, and say when it is for. The docs
theme toggle likewise showed "Dark" but was named "Switch to light
theme"; its name now starts with the visible word.

fix(nav): keep the chapter clear of the links; size the targets

The chapter label was absolutely centred on the window, so seven links
ran under it from 1360 to 1600px. Make it a flexible middle cell that
truncates instead. Give Menu and Close 44px square targets (they were
36x17), give links a 44px-tall hit area, and pad overlay numbers so the
tenth reads 10.

fix(home): make each selected piece a real disclosure button

The rows were articles with role=button, which flattens their heading
and isn't a valid role for article. Put a button inside each heading,
stretched over the row, with aria-expanded and aria-controls. Lay the
rows on one grid at every width so phones stop wrapping the meta and
arrow differently per row, set the year in the readable faint ink (it
was at 60%, 2.6:1), use the warm white of filled buttons for text on the
hover fill, and replace the hint with one that holds on touch and links
to the lab rather than the workshop.

fix(split-flap demo): let the keyboard scroll the departures board

On a phone the board scrolls sideways, but nothing in it can take focus,
so keyboard users couldn't reach the columns past the edge. Make the
scroller a named, focusable region.

fix(examples/nav): give the isolated nav a skip target and a title

The skip link pointed at #main, which this page lacked, and the tab
showed the site's default title. Name the main element and give the page
its own title; it stays out of the index.

fix(design-review): stop naming the contact sheet twice

The wrapping section and the Gallery inside it were both regions named
"All submissions". The Gallery's region is the one that matters; the
section is layout.

fix(examples): keep component headings under a section heading

Signature systems title themselves with h3, and on the example pages
they sat straight under the h1. Give each example a visually hidden h2
for its working area, and set the Plane demo's cluster titles as h3
under the page's h2 instead of h4.

fix(home): give the manifesto a heading

The manifesto's principles were h3s under the page's h1 with nothing in
between. Its section tag now renders as the h2.

feat(section-tag): let a tag be its section's heading

SectionTag always rendered a paragraph, so a section titled only by its
tag had no heading and the outline jumped a level. Add an as prop for
h2-h4, keep the paragraph default, and pin the weight so a heading looks
the same.

fix(wave-text): give screen readers the text, not an ignored label

The letters are aria-hidden and the word sat in aria-label on a span,
which assistive technology ignores on generic elements, so a span
WaveText was silent. Render the text in a visually hidden span instead.

fix(docs): label code regions and make guide snippets copyable

Component pages now name their usage, install and import blocks, and the
getting-started guide renders its sixteen snippets with CodeBlock, so
each has a copy action and a distinct name instead of sixteen regions
called "Code example".

feat(code-block): let each block name its region

Every CodeBlock was a region named after its language, so a page with
several listed identical landmarks. Add an optional label, falling back
to the filename and then the language, and document it.

fix(treemap): keep nested preview labels legible on hot blocks

Nested labels used the faint ink, which falls to 2.8-3.1:1 once heat
tints a block toward the accent. Mix them from paper at 78% instead,
above 4.5:1 on every heat in both themes.

fix(chronicle): fade unselected marks, not their labels

A selection set every other event to 0.42 opacity, labels included,
leaving 12px text at 3.2-3.7:1 against the lanes. Fade only the marks and
turn the labels muted, which keeps the focus and passes 4.5:1.

fix(toast): hold a toast while it is hovered or focused

Auto-dismissal ran regardless of attention, so a toast could disappear
mid-read or while its dismiss button had focus (WCAG 2.2.1). Hold the
timer on pointer enter and focus, restart it on leave and blur, and draw
the dismiss cross as an SVG instead of the × glyph.

fix(slider): announce the formatted value

With a format function the readout showed "40%" while assistive
technology announced the raw number. Pass the formatted text as
aria-valuetext.

fix(copy-button): name it by its label, not the copied text

The default aria-label was "Copy <text>", so a code block's button was
announced with the entire snippet. Let the visible label name it, fall
back to "Copy" when there is none, and extend the 17px-tall hit area
with an invisible margin.

fix(combobox): scroll the active option into view

The option list scrolls past 280px, but arrow keys moved the highlight
without scrolling, so it left the visible list. Scroll the next option to
the nearest edge as CommandPalette already does.

fix(tabs): select the first tab when none is chosen

Without a defaultValue no trigger was selected, so no panel rendered and
every trigger had tabindex -1, leaving the tablist out of the tab order.
TabsList now selects the first enabled tab whenever the value matches
none of its triggers.

fix(password-field): name the toggle by its action alone

The button changed its label between Show and Hide and also flipped
aria-pressed, so it announced "Hide password, pressed". Keep the action
label, drop the pressed state.

fix(search-field): keep focus in the field after clearing

The Clear button unmounts once the value is empty, so focus fell to the
body. Focus the input after clearing, and hide WebKit's own cancel button
so the field offers one clear action, not two.

fix(number-field): let a number be typed through the range

NumberField clamped every keystroke, so with min 10 typing 50 stopped at
10 after the 5, and clearing the field restored the old value. Keep the
typed text as a draft, report it once it is a number in range, and settle
it into range on blur or Enter.

fix(range-selector): put both handles on one shared scale

Each handle's native bounds follow the other handle, so the From slider's
track ran from min to the end value and the To slider's from the start
value to max. One number sat at different places on the two rows: on the
audio workbench a 0:17.3 start sat two thirds along its track and the
0:25.7 end a quarter along its own, so the end handle appeared left of the
start, and the page drew a separate ruler to show the real selection.

Each input now spans only the stretch of a shared scale it can reach,
placed with CSS custom properties, so both thumbs land where their values
fall and the selected window is drawn on both rows. The native min and
max, and so what assistive technology announces, are unchanged, and the
handles still cannot cross. The handles take Slider's hairline and
diamond, and the audio workbench drops its stand-in ruler.

docs: record the workshop QA pass and the bench page pattern

- WORKSHOP-TESTING: the browser pass now exists (1440, 820 and 375 px, both
  themes); Dock's pane keys are directional; block commands use the origin
  being browsed.
- README shows the deployed block install URL, with the local one as the
  alternative.
- CHANGELOG notes the Nav overlay fix, the one change to a released component.
- DESIGN.md records the bench page pattern so new benches start from it.
- The workshop brief reflects that the branch is now meant to land and push.

fix(nav): keep seven links reachable at every width

Adding Workshop made the primary links 714px wide, so between 768px and
about 850px they ran into the wordmark and past the right edge. The site
now switches to the menu below 900px.

The menu overlay could not scroll: seven 44px links are taller than many
phones, so Standpoint and Hire fell off the bottom of a 667px screen, and
Components was clipped at the right edge on narrow phones. The overlay now
scrolls with its close bar pinned, and link type steps down from 44px to
fit widths under 463px.

feat(workshop): give the workshop and blocks their own share cards

Every other section has an Open Graph card in the house style; the
workshop pages and /blocks fell back to the generic site image. The
workshop card covers the theme and playground benches too. The footer
index now lists the Workshop, matching the site navigation.

fix(forms): give DateRangeField presets a group and its actions room

The presets row carried a name on a plain div, which assistive technology
ignores; it is now a labelled group. Preset chips take the bright hairline
the rest of the library's chips and ghost controls use, instead of a line
barely darker than the page, and Clear and Reset sit 20px apart rather
than reading as one underlined phrase.

fix(dock): move tabs toward the pressed arrow

Alt + Shift with either arrow sent the focused tab to the other pane, so
Alt + Shift + → in the second pane moved the tab left. A move now happens
only when the arrow points at the other pane (→ from the first, ← from the
second), and the keymap says so.

The panel action row is a labelled group, since a name on a plain div is
not announced. The demo leaves a gap above Reset layout instead of butting
it against the dock, and its panels read as heading and note, like the
SplitPane demo.

fix(audio): keep the workbench readouts and divider honest

- The recording line said 00:51 while the player said 0:50; it now reads
  the duration from the bundled data in the transcript's clock format.
- The split handle sat in a pane aligned to the start, so its column was
  a 120px stub hanging between the transcript and the notes. It now runs
  the full height with its grip beside the panel headings.
- The playing passage is marked with the house selection bar instead of a
  vermilion wash.

fix(examples): number the audio workbench EX-04 everywhere

The index numbers its cards by position, and the audio workbench was
inserted third, so the index called it EX-03 (and automation EX-04) while
both pages said the opposite. It now comes last, matching EX-04 on its
page, lists its systems in the page's order, and the examples description
and share card name all four workflows.

fix(blocks): show file names as written and frame each block like a demo

- File names were Mizu ghost buttons, so the mono uppercase caption turned
  Readme.md into README.MD and the text sat on the button's left border.
  They are now plain selection buttons in the table's own type.
- Each block sits in a frame like the component demos: the install command
  and its copy action share the top bar, and the live block fills the stage
  beneath, instead of a floating code box with a copy link under it.
- The jump links move into the header as the examples' chips, removing the
  extra rule and the empty band above the first block.
- "Inspect registry source" becomes a labelled Registry JSON link that
  says it opens a new tab.
- Save and Discard stretch to one height; the ghost button's border made
  them differ by 2px.
- Showcase styles leave blocks.css, so installed blocks no longer copy the
  site's page layout into a project.
- The page title no longer reads "Blocks — Mizu compositions — Mizu".

fix(playground): write the JSX a person would write

Copied examples wrapped every string in an expression and listed every
default, so a button read
<Button variant="solid" size="md" ...>{"Keep the good work"}</Button>.
Plain text and attributes are now written as plain JSX, falling back to a
quoted expression only for characters JSX can't carry, and default props
are left out.

On component pages the inline controls now belong to that component: no
picker for the other four, no install note, and the bench keeps its two
columns instead of stacking the controls above the preview.

fix(workshop): tidy the theme and playground benches

- One copy action per export: the code block already copies, so the extra
  Copy CSS and Copy JSX buttons that sat above it are gone.
- Sliders in the control columns stack their track under the label, so the
  Corners and Initial value tracks span the column instead of ~50px.
- Reset links align with the fields; Narrow preview centres on its select.
- The preview's review list no longer draws a second rule under the tabs,
  and preview buttons keep their own width.
- Badge and Alert readouts no longer promise actions they don't have.

fix(workshop): set the index on fixed tracks with the house selection bar

Each index row sized its columns to its own action label, so the
descriptions started at a different x on every row. Rows now share fixed
tracks like the rate rows on /work: the 2px vermilion bar grows down the
left edge on hover or focus, and the action caption is a muted mono label
with an arrow instead of vermilion text, which is reserved for state.
Bench names follow the site's sentence case, and the workshop pages get
descriptive titles like the rest of the site.

fix(workshop): hold every bench to the examples container and header

The workshop shell centred itself with auto margins inside the flex body,
so each page shrank to its own content: the index, theme bench and
playground rendered at different widths, switching playground components
moved the whole page, and on phones the theme bench grew past the viewport
and was clipped. The shell now uses the examples container and header, and
its local navigation is the kicker line, with the current bench in accent.
fix(playground): preserve typed field content in copied examples
docs: connect workshop discovery and document testing and compatibility
feat(registry): ship installable blocks and catalog the new systems
feat(docs): add interactive prop playground with executable JSX export
feat(examples): add audio review workbench with real sample and excerpt notes
feat(workshop): add live theme builder with contrast checks and CSS export
feat(layout): add state-preserving dock workspace
feat(forms): add accessible native date range field
docs: define Mizu workshop implementation contract
chore: remove redundant site, test and usage comments
chore: prune package commentary and regenerate registry sources
chore: remove redundant tooling comments and generated headers

feat(work): count where briefs stop, and land home links on their rate

Analytics now gets the brief's funnel: brief_prefill when a rate row primes
it, brief_start on the visitor's first answer, brief_answer once per
question with its step, then brief_sent with the commission, budget and
timeline chosen, or brief_failed with the reason shown. A prefill never
counts as a start. Only question ids and choice values are sent, never
what someone typed; a test holds both.

Each rate row has an id, rate-<commission>, and a scroll margin, so the
home page's links land on their row under the nav.

feat(home): close the archive with what it costs to have it made

The home page reached /work only through "Hire" in the nav and the footer.
A fifth section, after the lab, says it plainly: everything on the site was
made by one person, who makes the same work for your product. Beside it,
the four commissions with their floors and weeks, read from the same
constant as /work, each linking to its row there, and a way to start a
brief.

feat(share): give every page its own link-preview card

Every link shared from the site showed the home page's image. Each section
now draws its own 1200×630 card at build time, in the site's own type and
material: the wordmark, a mono label, the page's heading with its serif
accent word where the page has one, one line in the page's words, and its
address. Each of the 127 component pages gets its name and the first
clause of its tagline, with the full tagline as alt text. The home page
keeps its designed preview.

The layout no longer pins twitter:image to the home preview, so Next copies
each page's own og:image into it.

Satori reads neither woff2 nor variable axes, so src/lib/og carries static
cuts: Archivo at the site's display width (118) and weight (900) and at 400,
with Instrument Serif italic and JetBrains Mono, all under the OFL.

fix(work): send briefs from a verified domain given alone

CONTACT_FROM set to just the verified domain made every send fail: Resend
needs an address in from, so each brief came back "didn't send". A value
without an @ now sends as Mizu Studio <briefs@that-domain>; an address is
used as given, and nothing still falls back to Resend's test sender.

docs(design): record the /work patterns; refresh the sidecar

DESIGN.md gains "Site surfaces": the drafting surface, the dimension-line
note, the step ruler, the rate row and the working-surface frame, with
where they live.

.impeccable/design.json predated the rewrite of DESIGN.md. Its colors now
carry their values from core.css (the frontmatter they pointed at is gone),
its shadow entry matches the one-soft-shadow rule, Reveal and the nav
chapter breakpoint match the code, the five patterns have snippets, and the
rules and do's and don'ts are DESIGN.md's own words.

fix(work): keep the proof board beside its list; flip the readout

On desktop the proof list runs about 750px past the board, which left the
right column empty. The board now sticks under the nav while the list
passes, as the brief's copy does, and sits in the flow on narrow screens.

The direction contract has the readout flip: each deploy the playhead
crosses now drops into the readout like a split-flap card. CSS only, and
off under reduced motion.

fix(studio): speak as one person

The close said "by people who care about the difference" and a principle
said "We design the machine", while /work says Mizu Studio is one person.
They now read "by one person who cares about the difference" and "Design
the machine, not the screenshot."

refactor(annotator): name the open thread's subject once

The thread popover read (draft ?? active)! three times in its props, and
jsx-ast-utils can't resolve a non-null assertion, so every lint run printed
"TSNonNullExpression could not be resolved". It is now one popover value,
narrowed by the condition that renders it. No behavior change.

fix(motion): hydrate reduced-motion components without a mismatch

useReducedMotion read the visitor's setting on the first render, which the
server can't know. Under reduced motion every component that renders
differently for it (Reveal, MaskLine, Chronicle and others) produced markup
that didn't match the server's, on 11 of the site's 137 pages, and React
keeps the server's attributes when they differ.

The hook now uses useSyncExternalStore: "no preference" while hydrating,
then a re-render with the setting, and it follows changes to it. Reveal's
start and end no longer depend on the setting, only its timing, so nothing
is left offset when the setting arrives after mount. The site's Hero, Index,
Cursor and the /work stage use the package hook instead of motion's.

A crawl of every sitemap page now finds no hydration errors with reduced
motion on or off.

fix(work): keep the loading sweep a hairline

The sweep across the skeleton had a zero-offset accent ring that thickened
it into a glow. Loading is a hairline. Also note why the brief's frame is
Frame's classes on a div: Frame renders a figure, and a form isn't one.

fix(work): let the proof be handled, not read

The proof board was a split-flap turning through system names, which still
only named the work. Now it shows three archive pieces working together: a
Knob and a Fader, and a SplitFlap board that settles on what they were set
to when they let go. You can drag them, use the arrow keys or double-click
to reset, and each one links to its page. The board sits at the top of the
section, beside the heading.

The Interview's question count is gone on /work. Its progress rule already
counts, and vermilion stays with action.

fix(work): act on the finish review

- Proof shows the archive working instead of only naming it: a bracketed
  split-flap board turns through the 22 signature systems, each a link
  away. It turns only on screen, and only by hand under reduced motion.
  The page passes just the names, so the catalog stays on the server.
- The sketch's notes are dimension lines with end ticks across each box,
  an annotated drawing rather than labelled rectangles.
- The step headings each carry one serif accent word. The "01 / 05"
  counters are gone: the stage's ruler and its Fig. label already carry the
  sequence, and vermilion goes back to action and selection, which includes
  the Interview's question count.
- The k floor moves into the first-person line, and the brief is signed.
- The rate card's columns are fixed tracks, so every row lines up.
- The brief sits in the stage's bracket frame, and its choices use the
  card's width.
- The chart's data runs to 24:00 to match its axis.
- The surface brief records why the headline is "Have it made.".

docs(work): set up the commission inbox; polish the brief's words

The README names the environment variables the brief needs and what happens
without them. The brief's messages use typographic apostrophes like the
rest of the page, and its confirmation sits at body weight under the bold
"It's in."

fix(studio): square "not a template shop" with taking commissions

"Nothing here is a starting point for someone else's idea" reads as a
refusal of client work now that Mizu takes commissions. The line now says
what a commission is: made for you, not filled in from a kit. The
manifesto's close offers /work beside the way back to the archive.

feat(nav): link /work as Hire from the nav and the footer

Hire is short enough to fit a sixth link. The nav's chapter label sits at
the center of the page, and with six links it would run into them below
1360px (measured with Commission, the longest chapter), so the site hides it
there. It already overlapped the links between 1024px and about 1230px.

feat(work): add the proof, the rates and the brief

- Proof: "Judge the work, not a logo wall." points at the three examples and
  every system in the archive. No client work is claimed.
- Rates: the four commissions on a rate card, cheapest first, each with its
  weeks, what's included and its floor. The whole row is the target of its
  "Brief this" button, which pre-selects that commission in the brief and
  moves focus to it. A line below names the work outside what's on offer.
- Brief: Mizu's own Interview asks seven questions and sends them through
  the server action. A failure keeps the answers, gives the reason, and

Button's spinner uses it, so the diamond is the label's warm white on

fix(styles): let your own CSS override Mizu's tokens in any load order

Mizu's tokens were unlayered rules on :root and [data-theme]. A registry
item's base.css loads after the app's global stylesheet, so in a fresh
Next.js app an override written where shadcn users write theirs,
`:root { --mizu-accent-fill: #2763c4 }` in globals.css, was silently
reset, and so was one on the element that carries data-theme="light".
It only held when the override happened to load later.

The token blocks now sit in `@layer theme`, the lowest layer. Any
unlayered rule beats them wherever it loads, and with Tailwind v4 they
join its own theme layer, below preflight and utilities, where a
`@layer base` override also wins. Tailwind v3 passes the layer through
untouched, and nothing but tokens moves: component rules stay unlayered,
so v3's unlayered preflight still can't undo them. The status colors
move up beside the other color tokens, one block per theme.

Checked in the shadcn-installed app: both overrides in globals.css now
apply (#2763c4 on :root, #6b2bd9 beside data-theme="light"), where the
defaults won before; the docs site compiles the tokens into Tailwind's
theme layer and builds unchanged. A test holds every token in the layer.

fix(docs): start browser examples with "use client"

Pasted into a fresh Next.js App Router page, as the catalog pages invite,
49 of the 126 usage examples broke: 37 failed to compile because they
call a hook (useState, useToast, useHistory) and 12 failed to render
because they hand a function to a component (DataTable's render,
AsyncButton's action, Treemap's format). The site never saw it: the
compiled demos live in one "use client" module.

examples:sync now derives the directive from each example's code and
writes it into usage.json. An example needs the browser when it calls a
hook or when a value it hands to JSX is, or holds, a function; helpers
it only calls, like Chronicle's date builder or a callback to
Array.from, stay on the server, so Mark, Stat and the other static
examples remain Server Components. Component pages say why the
directive is there and that other React setups ignore it.

Checked against a real app: every example pasted verbatim into its own
page of a create-next-app project with the shadcn-installed components
builds and prerenders, where 49 failed before. The analyzer flags
exactly those 49, and a test holds usage.json to it.

refactor: move components' static inline styles into mizu-* classes

Accordion, Tabs, Mark, Badge, Frame, Rule, SectionTag, CopyButton,
WaveText, MaskLine, Magnetic, PageWipe, Tilt and CountUp styled
themselves with inline style objects, so consumers could not restyle
them without !important, hover and focus rules could not reach them
(Accordion's title transitions a color that never changes), and the
registry shipped them no stylesheet. Their faces move into core.css:
tones as modifier classes (mizu-badge--accent), state through the
attributes the components already set (aria-expanded, aria-selected)
and data-copied. Sizes from props, Motion values and MaskLine's
reduced-motion will-change stay inline, and so does the caller's style,
which now overrides the defaults: Badge, Frame, Rule, SectionTag,
MaskLine and Magnetic used to drop conflicting properties. Each rule
ships once, in its module's stylesheet (Mark.css, which Badge, Rule,
SectionTag and CopyButton import); only Reveal, Presence and
MotionPreferences, which have no static styles, still bring base.css
alone.

Rendering is unchanged. Frame's brackets keep the frame's text color:
the inline shorthand always reset their accent border-color. PageWipe's
label loses a static opacity that Motion's keyframes always overwrote.
The newly classed elements are border-box like the rest of Mizu, so
Frame's corners are 9px without a global reset too, and disabled tabs
and copy buttons take the shared not-allowed cursor. The annotator
demo's page rule drops to zero specificity so it no longer resizes the
SectionTag inside it.

Checked against the parent commit on every docs page and the 404, dark
and light: computed styles and geometry of every element, open
accordion, switched tabs, copied button, reduced motion and a wipe
mid-sweep are identical, and the component pages screenshot
byte-identical above their install sentences, the only text that
changes.

fix(registry): ship each CSS rule once, in the module that owns it

Module stylesheets took every rule whose classes appeared anywhere in the
module's import closure, so shared pieces repeated: .mizu-sr-only sat in
29 files, .mizu-field-hint in 24, Button's and Dialog's rules in every
module that renders them; 1,945 selector copies for 1,350 selectors.
Beyond bytes, a later file's copy of a base rule undid earlier overrides:
with command-palette imported before dialog, a Next build gave the
palette Dialog's 36px 32px 32px padding, and trend-chart's copy of
.mizu-sig-scan cleared Chronicle's loading fill.

Each selector now ships once, in the stylesheet of its owner: the lowest
module that renders all of its classes and that every item needing it
imports. Barrels import base.css, then the shared stylesheets the item
renders, then every stylesheet in its closure, dependencies first, so an
override still loads after what it overrides. A selector list splits
only when no one module owns all of it. Classes unrelated modules render
(the field chrome, the data table, text-button, slider input) get one
stylesheet each under shared/, imported only by the items that render
them; putting them in base.css instead cost every item 4 KB.
.mizu-sr-only and .mizu-field-hint move to core.css's utilities, so
base.css carries them.

All registry CSS: 232.6 KB in 66 files becomes 171.0 KB in 70. Checked
every equal-specificity pair against the package order through the real
barrels: none that can share an element reverses; four from split
selector lists lose their guarantee only if a Checkbox nests in a
SegmentedControl or an InlineEdit in HistoryControls. Checked with
shadcn 4.21 (preset init, all 127 items) and a Next 16.3 production
build: each rule appears once, and the palette padding and loading fill
hold.
Move non-color CSS tokens to :root outside theme blocks

fix: keep pure helpers out of client modules; say what add copies

A constant exported from a "use client" module reaches server code as a
client reference, not a value: the reviewer's TICKER.map is not a
function. Mizu modelled the pattern itself. FLAP_CHARACTERS, flapPath,
justifyRows, tidyFlow, squarify and moveCard were declared in client
modules, and the package root exported describeQuery and matchesQuery
through QueryBuilder's. They move verbatim into plain sibling modules
(flap, justify, flow, squarify, cards), following query.ts and
outline.ts. Each component re-exports its helpers, which is the item API
the registry reads. The signature index exports them straight from the
plain modules, and explicit exports win over the components' export *.
The public names are unchanged.

Checked by prerendering a Server Component that calls the helpers, with
shadcn 4.21 and a production Next build. With the previous registry it
fails on "c.FLAP_CHARACTERS.split is not a function"; with the packed
previous package, on "Attempted to call justifyRows() from the server".
Both now render real values. Tarball consumer checks pass on React 18
and 19.

Two tests hold the rule. Every public non-component value must reach
the root without passing a client module. Module names must stay
distinct without extensions in any case, because gallery.ts beside
Gallery.tsx would collide in dist on macOS and Windows.

Docs now say exactly what `add` copies: base.css and the source
module's stylesheet, or base.css alone for the fifteen inline-styled
components such as Accordion. Every component page states which case
applies. Getting started and the README explain keeping server-read data
out of "use client" modules.

feat(registry): let static components render as Server Components

The generator wrote "use client" at the top of every item's file, so
Mark, Rule, Badge, Kbd, Stat, Timeline and every other static primitive
became a client reference: no server rendering, all their code in the
browser. The file gave no hint whether the component is interactive.

Item files now carry no directive; each source module keeps its own. 22
items (the ui primitives, content/Typography, data/Records, layout and
GhostWord) render on the server. Everything interactive stays a Client
Component through its source, and pure helpers keep their plain values.
Checked with shadcn 4.21 and a production Next build of a Server
Component page using Mark, Badge, Stat, Timeline, CodeBlock and Button:
its client-reference manifest lists only Button and CopyButton, the copy
control inside CodeBlock.

Every item's `meta.client` in registry.json, and each component page,
says which kind it is, read from the source directive.

The blanket directive had hidden that ui/Slider.tsx lacked its own
despite an input change handler, so Slider now declares "use client".
A catalog test holds every module without the directive to no hooks,
event handlers or context, and it fails on the old Slider.

feat(docs): make every import path its component's name

The reviewer guessed data-inspector for DataInspector, as the rule for
most components suggests, but eight older slugs broke it: copybutton,
countup, ghostword, maskline, pagewipe, ripplesurface, softtype and
wavetext. Those pages, registry items and import paths are now
copy-button, count-up, ghost-word, mask-line, page-wipe, ripple-surface,
soft-type and wave-text, and the old page URLs redirect with a 308.
define()'s kebab rule is now exported as slugOf, and a catalog test holds
every slug to it, so a hand-written slug can't drift again.

registry file `add` installs, and names the components that share its
source module with links, so the grouping in source/ shows where people
copy commands. Getting started and the README state the rule.

default theme) in the paragraph this edits.

feat(registry): name each item's exports instead of export *

Every item's file did `export * from "./source/<module>"`, so installing
knob also offered Fader and XYPad, tree-view offered DataInspector,
ActivityFeed and DiffView, and internals leaked (Dialog's lockScroll,
Preferences' useReducedMotion).

The generator now reads the package's public API with the TypeScript
checker, resolving each name to the module that declares it, and gives
each item its share of it. When the module serves one item, that is all
of the module's public exports. When items share a module, it is the
item's own component plus the public types its declaration mentions,
following the module's local helpers and types (knob: Knob and
ControlTaper; task-progress: TaskProgress and TaskStep; chronicle adds
Interval and SignatureTone from internal). Statements are grouped by
declaring module, so QueryBuilder's pure helpers come from ./query and
never pass through a client module. Generation throws when a shared
module's public value or type belongs to no item.

Every barrel value is public, and every public value is in a barrel,
except the motion easings and useCanvasLoop, which no barrel exposed
before. Typecheck compiles all 127 barrels against the mirrored source.
In a shadcn-installed app, `import { Fader } from ".../knob"` is now
TS2305.

fix(registry): ship one stylesheet per source module

Styles were generated per item from the item's source closure, so every
item sharing a module got a byte-identical copy: the 11 status/Feedback
items (alert, progress, meter, skeleton, status…) each shipped the same
3.5 KB file, and 11 more module groups did the same (forms/Fields ×8,
content/Typography ×6, navigation/Navigation ×6…). Installing several
items put several identical files in the repo, and the bundler, seeing
different paths, bundled each one.

The stylesheet is now keyed on the source module and written beside it,
source/status/Feedback.css, and every item's barrel imports that one file.
Class collection takes the union of the module's catalog examples, so no
item loses a rule. 116 items get byte-identical styles and 12 gain only
.mizu-field-hint. Checked with shadcn 4.21 and a production Next build:
alert, progress and meter now install one Feedback.css, and the CSS
bundle holds a single .mizu-alert rule.

112 per-item files become 64 module files; all registry CSS goes from
386 KB to 233 KB.

Getting started told people to run bare `npx shadcn@latest init`. In an
existing project that installs shadcn's default style: it rewrites
globals.css (new imports, OKLCH neutral tokens replacing the project's,

lucide-react and cva, and records base-nova, neutral and lucide in

With next/font, a face registers under a hashed family, not "Archivo

variables and they apply, set on <html> or <body>, with nothing to

Feature the signature systems on the home page

A new "Signature systems" section indexes all twenty-two systems in
their collection order, each a link to its page with the first clause of
its tagline, and points to the composed examples. The lab section
becomes 04.

Add composed examples: incident review, design review, automation

Three whole workflows, each sharing one state across several signature
systems, under a new Examples section in the site navigation:

- Incident review: Chronicle, two TrendCharts and LogStream share one
  moment and one zoom window; the focus panel reads the time on a
  SplitFlap and lists what was happening. The charts are derived from
  the same invented service's logs, now a shared harbour module.

Action buttons that neither navigate nor leave the page no longer carry
the outbound arrow.

Let LogStream bring a line chosen elsewhere into view

When `selected` changes from outside, such as a synchronised timeline,
the chosen line scrolls into view, and the tail stops pulling the view
to the newest line while one is open.

Add Knob, Fader and XYPad, controls for instruments rather than forms

Each drawn control stands on native range inputs, so keyboards, screen
readers and forms work without extra wiring (a named control submits its
real value, even on a log taper). Knobs drag vertically and faders by
their cap, with Shift for fine adjustment, a tenth of the range on
Shift-arrows and Page keys, and double-click or Backspace to return
home. Log tapers spread ratios evenly for frequencies and times. Values
spring to discrete changes and follow the hand directly while dragging.

Faders take a live level, as a number or a motion value for re-render
free metering, with instant attack, steady release and a held peak. The
XY pad springs its puck to a press, trails a comet while dragging, and
exposes each axis as its own slider with 2-D arrows from either.

The showcase plays a real WebAudio voice whose meters and scope read the
audio graph, and grades a plate with a form that exports its settings.

Add LogStream, a live tail you can stop, search and read

Only the lines in view are rendered, so a bounded window of thousands of
lines scrolls freely. The tail follows new lines until you scroll away;
then a count of missed lines springs up and is announced at most every
five seconds, and positions are tracked by line id so trimming the
window never skews it. Levels filter with live counts, search highlights
matches and steps through them, and a stacked overview strip shows
volume and trouble over time and jumps to any moment. A chosen line
opens whole with its fields in DescriptionList, and `selected` can be
controlled to sync with a chart or timeline.

Add ColumnBrowser, Miller columns that load as you walk them

Choosing an item opens its contents in the next column until a leaf
opens in a preview. Children can arrive lazily through loadChildren:
loading columns sweep a hairline over skeleton rows, results are kept,
and failures reuse ErrorState with a retry. Arrows walk within and
across columns with one tab stop for the whole browser, typing jumps to
a name, and focus follows moves into columns that have only just
rendered. Below 520px of container width the columns become a stack
that pushes and pops, with a back button that names its destination.

The showcase browses an invented project (with a folder that fails
once) and an organisation composed from Avatar, Badge and
DescriptionList.

Add SplitFlap, a display where every character falls into place

Each cell falls forward through its drum like the real mechanism: the top
leaf folds down and darkens while the next character lands with a small
overshoot, and neighbouring cells start a beat apart so a change ripples
down the line. Flips are Web Animations written straight to the DOM, so a
whole board flipping costs no React renders. Long journeys skip ahead to
the last dozen flaps, and reduced motion shows the value at once.

Assistive technology reads the value as text beside the hidden cells;
live displays announce each settled value once. The showcase runs an
invented departures board, a message board and a flip clock.

Add Folio and Sidenote, long-form reading with notes in the margin

Sidenotes sit in the margin level with their mark (their static position
does the aligning) and step down just far enough to clear each other,
gliding when the text reflows. Below 880px of container width they fold
into the text and unfold beneath their line. A contents rail built from
the headings follows the reader, marks the section in view, fills with
progress and counts down the reading time; choosing a section moves
focus there.

The docs preview stage now clips horizontally instead of scrolling, so
sticky parts of a demo follow the page.

Add Gallery, photos that open from where they sit

A justified grid (rows fill the width at the height nearest a target,
bounded so a panorama never crushes its neighbours) whose photos fly out
of their tile into a native modal viewer and back into the tile of
whichever photo you close on. Swipe or arrow keys travel, pulling down
dismisses as the backdrop thins, and pinch, Ctrl-scroll or double-tap
zoom around the point under your fingers with bounded panning.

Dialog's scroll lock is now a shared lockScroll() so both modals stack
correctly. The showcase draws its landscape plates in the browser, so the
docs need no network images.

Add TriageDeck, decisions at the speed of a gesture

The top card follows the hand and tilts with it; decision stamps fade
in past a threshold, and release offset or velocity flings it off
toward left, right or up with a spring carrying that velocity. The
stack steps forward in depth, and undo flies the card back from the
side it left by. Arrow keys and labelled buttons make the same
decisions; tallies count them, every decision announces what happened
and what comes next, and Backspace undoes. Reduced motion decides
without flight or tilt.

The shared seal keyframes move into signature.css so no component's
stylesheet depends on another's.

Add TransferQueue, uploads you can watch and steer

A concurrency-limited runner around your own transfer function: files
arrive through the existing FileDropzone (or the add() handle), each
receives an AbortSignal and an onProgress callback, and progress is
batched to one update per frame. Speed is smoothed, time left is
estimated per file and overall, and a Sparkline traces throughput.
Pause aborts (resume restarts unless your function continues from an
offset), failures keep their reason with a retry, and cancel aborts
and removes. Hairlines change colour with state and a check diamond
pops on completion.

The usage example reads files locally in chunks, so the live render
does real work without sending anything anywhere.

Add Interview, a conversational one-question-at-a-time form

Questions rise in going forward and settle back going back, each with
its own labelled form and focus. Choices answer with letter keys and a
single choice confirms with a double blink before moving on; yes/no
takes Y and N, scores take digits, long answers take Ctrl+Enter.
Required answers, email shape, numeric bounds and custom validators
reject with a linked alert and one shake. next(answers) branches, the
review lists every answer with an edit jump, and onSubmit is followed
honestly: loading, a retry that keeps everything, then completion.

Add Tour, a spotlight that travels between real elements

A native modal dialog draws a veil with a spotlight hole framed by
accent corner brackets. The target is measured every frame while the
tour is open, so scrolling, resizing and reflow never detach it; after
a step change the spotlight pursues the element even while it scrolls
into view. The card takes the preferred side if it fits, otherwise the
roomiest, points with a diamond notch, docks as a bottom sheet on
phones and centres with an explanation when a step's element is
missing. Steps are announced, arrows move between them, focus stays on
the primary action and returns to the trigger; onFinish only fires when
the last step is completed.

Give the signature editors one data and editing contract

Board and FlowGraph now accept controlled data or uncontrolled
defaults (cards / defaultCards, nodes / defaultNodes, edges /

Add Annotator, review pins and threads on any surface

Wrap an image, a page or a live composition to review it: comment mode
(C) drops a numbered diamond pin where you click, or at the centre with
Enter, and Alt+arrows move it while you write. Threads unfold beside
their pin and rise from pins low on the work; they carry replies,
resolve and reopen, and return focus to their pin on Escape. Pins drag
or nudge with arrow keys and store rounded fractional positions. The
list beside the work offers every thread without the surface and
collapses beneath it on narrow screens. Read-only when no author is
given.

Add QueryBuilder, conditions that read as a sentence

Fields declare a type and receive fitting operators and inputs: text,
numbers with units and ranges, dates and "in the last N days", selects
as chips (or the existing MultiSelect for long lists) and booleans.
Groups nest to a limit and switch between all and any through the
existing SegmentedControl; the and/or joins roll over like a counter.
Incomplete conditions are described and ignored rather than emptying
results. describeQuery gives the plain-language reading shown in serif
beneath the editor, and matchesQuery evaluates records for local
filtering — the showcase filters accounts through DataTable live.

Add Outliner, a keyboard-first outline you can zoom into

Enter splits at the caret (a new first child under an open parent),
Tab and Shift+Tab restructure with descendants, outdenting follows the
parent's whole subtree so later siblings stay put, Alt+arrows move a
branch, modifier chords mark lines done or fold them, and Backspace at
the start merges upward. Every operation is a pure function over flat
rows rebuilt into a tree, with its own tests.

Diamond bullets show folded and done states, hairline guides sit under
ancestor bullets and the active thread is traced in accent. Focusing
into an item turns its text into the page title through a shared
layout transition, with a location trail back out.

Add Board, a kanban with lift-and-carry dragging

Cards lift into a tilted ghost that shares its layout id with the list
slot, so a drop flies the card from the hand into place while the
column parts to make room; carried near an edge, the board scrolls.
Mouse drags start anywhere on a card, touch drags from a grip so the
page still scrolls. Columns show counts, advisory limits in words, fold
into a vertical strip and can offer an add action.

The keyboard path picks up with Space, carries with arrows across
positions and columns, drops with Space and restores with Escape, with
assertive announcements at each step; focus follows the card when it
remounts in another column. moveCard is exported for custom commands.
Hoist Treemap's layout helper so its memo lists real dependencies

Add Treemap, a hierarchy by size you enter like a place

Squarified blocks sized by value (the exported squarify is reusable),
with nested previews of the next level, tone stripes and optional heat.
Opening a block is a camera move: the entering level is laid out for the
stage and squeezed into the block, so the flight lands exactly on the
final arrangement while neighbours fly outward; only geometry animates,
so text never distorts. Returning plays the path in reverse.

Arrow keys travel to the nearest block in each direction, Enter opens
or chooses, Backspace returns, openings are announced and focus lands on
the largest block inside. A readout reports value and shares instead of
floating tooltips.

Add Plane, an infinite canvas, and FlowGraph, a node editor on it

Plane is a zoomable surface: drag with inertia, pinch or Ctrl-scroll at
the pointer, a zoom-adaptive grid, a minimap and a camera handle (fit,
zoomBy, flyTo, toWorld). Plain scrolling pans only once the canvas is
active, so embedded canvases never trap the page. Tabbing to an item
flies the camera to it; long flights pull back before settling in.
Content can adapt to scale through --mizu-plane-zoom and data-scale.

FlowGraph wires nodes on a Plane: fixed port metrics keep edges exact
without measurement, outputs snap magnetically to the nearest input,
and Enter on an output then an input wires from the keyboard. Callers
validate connections; loops and duplicates are refused as alerts.
Running nodes scan and send flowing dashes down their wires, selection
brackets snap in, far zoom counter-scales titles, and Tidy (or the
exported tidyFlow) animates the graph into layered order.

Share one interval and tone vocabulary across the time systems

TrendChart's visible window is now range / defaultRange / onRangeChange,
matching Chronicle, and both use the exported Interval and
SignatureTone types, so linked views pass values without adapters.
Waveform bars now rise from silence rather than printing left to right,

Add Waveform, an audio scrubber you can see

A waveform slider over a native audio element: supplied peaks or peaks
decoded from the source (with a gentle gamma so quiet passages read),
pointer scrubbing with a hover preview, markers mirrored in a chapter
list with durations, speed and skip controls, a play glyph that morphs
to pause, and a handle with play, pause and seek for external controls
such as transcripts. Decoding, flat and failed sources each have a state.

The showcase composes a 48-second pentatonic piece offline with Web
Audio, so it plays real audio without shipping a file.

Add TrendChart, a measuring instrument for values over time

A live legend reads every series at the crosshair, so no tooltip covers
the data. Dragging (or Shift + arrows) measures a period and reports
each series' change, percentage and peak; Enter or "Zoom to period"
glides there. Annotations, threshold lines, null gaps, a table view and
controlled cursor/domain props let several charts read and zoom as one.

responsive without losing peaks.
